To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antiemetic drug research and development is challenging, that emetogenic classification of new antineoplastics is difficult and that nausea control is an emerging problem.

antiemetic agents can be tested using the same principles as other antineoplastic drugs, that the emetogenicity level of a new antineoplas-tic agent must be determined in the absence of antiemetic prophylaxis, and that nausea control must be considered in parallel with vomiting control.

the emetic effects of new antineoplastics should be determined using the MASCC/ESMO classification, and the emetogenicity and efficacy of new antiemetics should be determined using a validated scale such as MASCC Antiemetic Tool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs and the improvement of antiemetic regimens.
the development of antiemetics for the treatment of chemotherapy-induced vomiting and nausea.
the evaluation of new antiemetics in the prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

antiemetic agents are effective, that antiemetic drug research and development should be encouraged, that emetogenicity should be accurately reported, and that the challenge of nausea should be addressed.
antiemetic agents are now so effective that they are no longer considered “supportive care” but are now considered to be part of the antineoplastic regimen itself.

the development of antiemetic agents is in a mature state, and that the next logical steps are to identify optimal combinations of agents, to identify optimal regimens of administration, and to develop agents for the control of nausea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MASCC/ESMO consensus conference on the classification of emetic risk has been a useful step forward in the field, and that the MASCC and ESMO societies have made a valuable contribution by providing the framework to facilitate further discussion and research in this field.
we have come a long way but still have a long way to go.
the MASCC/ESMO expert panel has established a framework for antiemetic drug and antineoplastic emetogenicity classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emetogenicity classification of the 2009 MASCC/ESMO Consensus Conference is a useful tool for antiemetic drug developers.
antiemetic therapy has been remarkably successful, but that further progress will require new approaches to antiemetic drug evaluation.
the MASCC/ESMO emetogenicity scale is a useful tool to guide antiemetic drug selection and to guide the design of antiemetic clinical trials.
